cards.definition: To give people a particular impression of yourself.
cards.example:
- In interviews, I want to come across as confident and prepared, never arrogant.
Em entrevistas, quero passar a impressão de confiante e preparado, nunca arrogante.
cards.note: Estrutura: come across as + adjetivo: He comes across as rude. Sem o as, come across = encontrar por acaso.

cards.definition: A comfortable connection between people who understand each other.
cards.example:
- Good salespeople build rapport in the first minutes, long before they talk about price.
Bons vendedores criam sintonia nos primeiros minutos, muito antes de falar de preço.
cards.note: O “t” é mudo: /ræˈpɔːr/. Colocação fixa: build rapport with someone.

cards.definition: The way you look and behave, especially under pressure.
cards.example:
- Her calm demeanor during the crisis impressed the whole executive panel.
A postura calma dela durante a crise impressionou toda a banca executiva.
cards.note: Palavra elegante para descrever pessoas: a calm/professional demeanor. No inglês britânico, demeanour.

cards.definition: Confident, without needing approval from others.
cards.example:
- She sounded self-assured even when the investors asked difficult questions.
Ela soou segura de si, mesmo quando os investidores fizeram perguntas difíceis.
cards.note: Um degrau acima de confident no registro. O substantivo é self-assurance.

cards.definition: To look directly into someone's eyes while speaking.
cards.example:
- Try to make eye contact with everyone in the room, not only the decision-maker.
Tente fazer contato visual com todos na sala, não só com quem decide.
cards.note: O verbo é make, nunca “do”: make eye contact with someone.

cards.definition: What your posture and movements say without words.
cards.example:
- Your body language often says more about you than your words do.
Sua linguagem corporal costuma dizer mais sobre você do que as suas palavras.

cards.translation: vestir-se à altura do papel / da ocasião
cards.definition: To wear clothes that match the role you want people to see.
cards.example:
- If you want to lead the project, dress the part at the next client meeting.
Se você quer liderar o projeto, vista-se à altura na próxima reunião com o cliente.
cards.note: Existe também look the part (parecer à altura do papel).

cards.translation: conquistar alguém / ganhar a confiança de alguém
cards.definition: To gain someone's support or trust, often gradually.
cards.example:
- Her honesty and careful preparation won the most skeptical clients over.
A honestidade e a preparação cuidadosa dela conquistaram os clientes mais céticos.
cards.note: Separável: win the client over ou win over the client. Muito usada em vendas e negociação.

cards.definition: Showing that you understand and care about someone's problem.
cards.example:
- My manager was very sympathetic when I explained the problem behind the delay.
Meu gestor foi muito compreensivo quando expliquei o problema por trás do atraso.
cards.note: “Simpático” NÃO é sympathetic — é friendly, nice ou likeable.

cards.definition: Having had a good education; well informed.
cards.example:
- She is a highly educated economist, with two master’s degrees and a PhD.
Ela é uma economista muito instruída, com dois mestrados e um doutorado.
cards.note: “Educado” (com boas maneiras) é polite ou well-mannered.

questions.prompt: In interviews I want to come across _____ confident, never arrogant.
questions.explanation: “Come across AS” + adjective or noun phrase.

questions.prompt: Good salespeople do this in the first minutes. They…
questions.explanation: Rapport is BUILT, slowly. “Make rapport” does not collocate.

questions.prompt: Her calm _____ during the crisis impressed the whole panel.
questions.explanation: “Demeanor” is how you carry yourself, especially under pressure.

questions.prompt: She sounded _____ even when the investors asked difficult questions.

questions.explanation: “Make eye contact WITH” a person — and it is “make”, not “do”.

questions.prompt: Sua linguagem corporal costuma dizer mais sobre você do que as suas palavras.
questions.answer: Your body language often says more about you than your words do.|Your body language often says more about you than your words.
questions.explanation: “Body language” is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

questions.prompt: If you want the promotion, _____ before you get it.
questions.explanation: “Dress the part” is to look like the role you are aiming at.

questions.prompt: The board was against it, and slowly she gained their support. She…
questions.explanation: Separable: the pronoun goes in the middle. Past of “win” is “won”.

questions.prompt: The manager understood your problem and refunded the night. He was…
questions.explanation: “Sympathetic” is understanding about a problem. The Portuguese “simpático” is “nice” or “friendly”.

options: She is highly educated: two degrees and a PhD.
He is very educated: he always says thank you.
She was educated with the waiter.
He is educated at the table.
questions.answer: She is highly educated: two degrees and a PhD.
questions.explanation: “Educated” is about schooling. Good manners is “polite” or “well-mannered”.
